subject: different z- an p-values in summary() an standardizedSolution()

messages.author: d2ed4b9cfef6304a
messages.subject: different z- an p-values in summary() an standardizedSolution()
parts:
Hello!

I created a meditiation model using the sem() function of lavaan. Now I'd like to report the standard errors of my standardized estimates and found the standardizedSolution() function. 
But I'm uncertain about the output of this function, because it shows different z- and p-values for the estimates (compared to those in the summary() fuction), which I wouldn't suspect. Isn't it so, that standardization (of both independent an dependent variables) shouldn't have an effect on z- and p-value?

My Code:
medg_fit <- sem(medg, data = d, meanstructure = T, estimator="MLR")
summary(medg_fit, fit.measures=TRUE, rsquare = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
## example output row
## -0.167 (Estimate) 0.077 (Std.Err) -2.173 (z-value) 0.030 (P(>|z|)) -0.167 (Std.lv) -0.115 (Std.all)
standardizedSolution(medg_fit, type = "std.all", se = TRUE, zstat = TRUE,
                     pvalue = TRUE, ci = TRUE, level = 0.95,
                     output = "pretty")
## example output row
## -0.115 (est.std) 0.053 (Std.Err) -2.184 (z-value) 0.029 (P(>|z|)) -0.219 (ci.lower) -0.012 (ci.upper)

I'd very much appreciate help! Thanks in advance!
Lina D

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: different z- an p-values in summary() an standardizedSolution()
parts:
Hi, Lina. The standardized estimates are the same in both functions.

In the summary, it is the last column (-0.115 (Std.all))

In the standardizedSolution, it is the first column (-0.115 (est.std)).

Best,
Yago

messages.author: b6ae83467b372bc6
messages.subject: Re: different z- an p-values in summary() an standardizedSolution()
parts:
Hello Linda,

as Yago already mentioned, with the standardizedSolution you obtain the completely standardized values; also, the p-, z-, as well as se-values for the standardized solution. Use the latter ones if you report the std. model results.

Marcus
